questions.explanation_english: The resistance change factor per degree celcius of temperature change is called the temperature coefficient of resistence. This factor is represented by the Greek lower case letter alpha (α). * Thermosistors are non-linear resistors, which alter resistance characterstics with temperature. The resistance of thermistors will decrease with the temperature increases. * The pure semicanductors and insulating material are having a negative temperature coefficient of resistance. Therefore, the resistance of semicanductors and insulators decreases with rising in temperature. Temperature coefficient of resistance of a doped semiconductor positive or negative depending on the level of doping. * The resistance tungsten increases with temperature.

questions.explanation_english: Nucleons in the nucleus of an atom are bonded together by a strong force of attraction called nuclear force. The nuclear force is short-ranged force that acts when nucleons are at distance in the range of fermi (1 fermi = 10–15 m). The nuclear force acts between proton-proton, proton- neutron and neutron-neutron. The force is so strong that it overcomes the electrostatic force of repulsion between proton - proton (like charges). The strength of the force is the same between any of the two nucleons. So, the order of nuclear forces strength is n n p p p n − = − = −

(B) S-phase (Synthesis) - DNA replication take place during this phase. During this time the amount of DNA per cell doubles. If the initial amount of DNA is denoted as 2C then it increases 4C. (C) G2 phase – Cell grows, make organelles & proteins. Cell also begins to reorganise its genetic content in preparation for mitosis. (D) M - phase - Cell divides its DNA and cytoplasm. (E) G0 phase – Cell exits from cell cycle and goes into quiscent stage. That means cell will not perform division in future. G1, S, G2 phases together are known as Interphase. During these phases cell prepares itself for mitosis. YCT DSSSB TGT Natural Science 2014 13 YCT

Leptotene - During leptotene, the chromatin condenses to form the chromosomes. Chromosomes are the longest and thinnest in this stage. Pachytene - Non-sister chromatids of the homologous chromosomes exchange their genetic parts (crossing over). Diplotene - X- shaped structure called chiasmata is clearly visible in this stage.

questions.question_english: A plant tissue from the hypodermal region of a young dicot stem possesses elongated living cells with uneven thickening at the corner. How do you recognize this tissue ?

questions.explanation_english: The collenchyma occurs in layers below the epidermis in most of the dicotyledonous plants. It is found either as a homogenous layer or in patches. It consists of cells that are much thickened at the corners due to deposition of cellulose, hemicellulose and pectin. Collenchyma cells are living cells, they may be oval, spherical or polygonal and often contain chloroplasts. These cells assimilate food when they contain chloroplasts. Inter cellular spaces are absent. They provide mechanical support to the growing parts of the plant such as the young stem and petiole of a leaf.

questions.question_hindi: कोशिका चक्र के दौरान निम्न में से क्या उ१ अवस्था की भूमिका उत्तम तरीके से स्पष्ट कर सकता है?
options_english: Cell grows and carries out normal metabolism
Cell grows and prepares for mitosis
options_hindi: कोशिका विकसित होती है और सामान्य चयापचय करती है

questions.explanation_english: Cell cycle is the formation of new cells from old ones. All the phases in cell cycle are equally important. There are 5 phases at all - (A) G1 phase – During the G-1 phase, the cell is metabolically active and continuosly grows but does not replicate it DNA. The cell grows maximum in the G1 phase. (B) S-phase (Synthesis) - DNA replication take place during this phase. During this time the amount of DNA per cell doubles. If the initial amount of DNA is denoted as 2C then it increases 4C. (C) G2 phase – Cell grows, make organelles & proteins. Cell also begins to reorganise its genetic content in preparation for mitosis. (D) M - phase - Cell divides its DNA and cytoplasm. (E) G0 phase – Cell exits from cell cycle and goes into quiscent stage. That means cell will not perform division in future. G1, S, G2 phases together are known as Interphase. During these phases cell prepares itself for mitosis. YCT DSSSB TGT Natural Science 2014 13 YCT

(E) G0 phase – Cell exits from cell cycle and goes into quiscent stage. That means cell will not perform division in future. G1, S, G2 phases together are known as Interphase. During these phases cell prepares itself for mitosis. YCT DSSSB TGT Natural Science 2014 13 YCT

questions.question_english: Which of the following organism is an example for saprophytic nutrition?

questions.explanation_english: Saprophytic Nutrition - In this type of nutrition the organisms depend on the dead and decaying matter of other organisms for their food. Fungi show the saprophytic mode of nutrition. The fungi like Rhizopus, Penicillium, Mucor and yeast are the other example of Saprophytes.
